newsitem.title: INDIA: India call easy despite auction outflows, gilts up.
newsitem.headline: India call easy despite auction outflows, gilts up.

text.p: Indian call money rates eased to 0.15-0.50 percent at close of trade on Tuesday, off opening quotes of 0.75-1.0 percent, dealers said.
They said a brief spurt of demand in early trade kept rates high before rates retreated to familiar territory.
Call money rates have been in a 0.10-0.50 percent range for the past two weeks.
Call money rates were easy despite outflows to repo and bond auctions held on Monday.
In separate auctions, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sold 10-year bonds for 30 billion rupees and accepted bids for 41.30 billion rupees at a four-day repo auction of government securities.
There was however little impact on liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected call money rates to remain range-bound at curent levels till liquidity was drained away from the banking system through government bond issues.
Dealers said prices of government securities rose in active trade on Tuesday with volumes on the National Stock Exchnage leaping to 8.5 billion rupees from Monday's 3.59.
A 60 basis point reduction in yield to 13.05 percent on the 10-year bonds at Monday's auction also fuelled demand for longer maturity securities, dealers said.
They said the newly-auctioned bond attracted heavy buying interest and was traded at prices between 100.50 rupees and 101.80 rupees against its auction price at par.
The 13.80 percent 2002 stock traded at 107.80 rupees compared to its last traded price of 106.90 rupees while the 13.55 percent 2001 rose to 107.25 from 105.70, dealers said.
Treasury bills were also actively traded with the bills maturing in April 1998 yielding 8.70 percent and 8.60 percent against the previous 8.70 percent, dealers said.
